question: Does replaying the Gemma 4 decode step from the whole-step HIP graph close the one trailing ladder depth (512-token decode at 0.96x of llama.cpp)?
hardware: AMD Radeon 8060S Graphics (gfx1151, Strix Halo), 126976 MiB unified memory
execution_profile: production for hipEngine (whole-step decode graph replay from the second per-token forward, default on; launched fallback for replay windows reaching the decode split route at 1024 keys); llama.cpp shipped HIP graph path, rows reused from 2026-10-08 unchanged

protocol.prompt_identity: same frozen campaign prompt IDs as the 2026-10-08 ladder's 512 row, so the comparator row pairs directly
protocol.hipengine_side: scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py instrumented path drives the production route: graph replay from decode forward 2, launched step 0 as the capture warm
protocol.comparator_side: llama.cpp HIP 17252c769 decode row reused unchanged from the 2026-10-08 paired ladder artifact

hipengine.source_note: measured on the working tree that became this commit (bench recorded the parent c0236a7b7 with dirty=true); the tree bytes equal the committed unit

correctness.production_ab_ids_equal: 128/128 greedy IDs identical between HIPENGINE_GEMMA4_DECODE_GRAPH=0 and default through hipengine.LLM.generate
correctness.deep_fallback: 1024-prompt session steps all take the launched fallback (0 captures) and are bit-identical to launched; 2048-prompt production run: 0 captures, 62 fallbacks, clean output

result.interpretation: The 512-token decode deficit was host-side launch overhead (~505 kernel launches per step, ~11 of 29.7 ms; rocprofv3 census 2026-10-09), not kernel time. Replaying the step's launches from a whole-step HIP graph removes the submission gaps; replay is bit-identical by construction and the guard excludes split-route windows where capture would bake host-computed slice geometry (measured ~10 percent relative logit divergence pre-guard). Every ladder depth now leads llama.cpp in decode.

mechanism.census: rocprofv3 kernel trace at restored 512-token state: ~505 launches/step, device kernel time ~18.7 ms vs ~29.7 ms wall
mechanism.graph: hipengine/runtime/gemma4_decode_graph.py whole-step capture (BUCKET_WIDTH 64), production wiring in hipengine/generation/gemma4_gguf.py
